newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold exchange volume jumps, prices mixed.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold exchange volume jumps, prices mixed.

text.p: Volume rose sharply in the morning session on the Istanbul gold exchange on Tuesday as banks competed to become the year's largest trader on the exchange, dealers said.
Total volume stood at 1,692 kg, up sharply from 785 kg on Monday.
Dollar prices were barely changed at $369.30 an ounce.
No dollar deals were made in the afternoon.
Lira prices rose to 1,270,250 lira per gram from a previous 1,267,500 due to the weakness of the lira, dealers said.

"The banks wanted to show the greatest volume for the year and so competition between them led to extra demand. Activity died down in the afternoon because of uncertainty caused by the central bank's dollar sales for lira," one dealer said.
The Turkish lira eased to 106,740 against the dollar from Monday's 106,560 close, despite central bank intervention in the afternoon, but firmed from an earlier low of 106,930.
Morning volume was 1,627 kg, including 1,070 kg of dollar-term trade, but plunged to 65 kg in the second session when no dollar deals were made.
Some 63.2 percent of the total daily turnover was recorded in dollar terms.
